title: Positive character weights at an affine rational fixed point
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $F$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its affine $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Give $X$ an action of $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga], that is, an $F$-scheme morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_F X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws. For an $F$-algebra map $\varepsilon:A\to F$, set $\mathfrak m=\ker\varepsilon$ and $T=\operatorname{Hom}_F(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2,F)$. For $v\in T$, its dual-number point [def-sc-dual-numbers] sends $a\in A$ to $\varepsilon(a)+v(\overline{a-\varepsilon(a)})\epsilon$. Its scalar extension to any commutative $F$-algebra $R$ is obtained by the coefficient map $F[\epsilon]\to R[\epsilon]$. Define positive tangent character weights at $\varepsilon$ to mean the existence of $d\geq0$, an $F$-basis $(v_i)_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)}$ of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and positive integers $n_i$ such that, for every commutative $F$-algebra $R$, every $g\in\mathbf G_m(R)$ and every $i$, the action of the constant lift of $g$ on the dual-number point of $v_i$ equals the point obtained by replacing $\epsilon$ by $g^{n_i}\epsilon$. These are identities of scheme-valued points over all algebras, hence character weights rather than differentials of characters. The empty basis $d=0$ and the zero test algebra are allowed. A fixed-point hypothesis is supplied separately by consumers.
